items.issues: D is the only nuanced/two-stage option (doubt→compassion), so pattern-savvy students can guess it by form; distractors A/B/C each contradict a clear textual cue.
B (disrepair blame) has no textual hook at all; A is the only mixed-tone option. Easy.
Poem states gratitude almost explicitly ('I lose to him slowly, with great care'); A/C/D are flat contradictions. Easy.
'a little grudgingly' nearly paraphrases C; C is the only mixed option. Clean but easy.
A is a reasonable trap (embarrassment in public), but 'too grateful' settles it. Solid medium.
B is a half-truth trap (she did laugh) but the apology undoes it; C/D weak. Easy-medium.
'with a wink' and 'red-faced' make C near-explicit; C is again the only mixed option. Easy.
B is a good anecdote-summary partial; C reverses the lesson; D over-generalizes. Meets the medium recipe.
A/B are detail-level partials, D moralizes beyond text. Clean; closer to easy-medium.
D ('never too late to learn') is supported by the seventy-year-old learner and some students will defend it; A is stronger because the mutual map/notebook exchange dominates, but D is a near-miss.
Handle-first hammer plus keeping Devon's bow curve make A obvious; D has no textual support. Easy.
A (forgiveness) is partially defensible since the handshake could carry both; B is better anchored by 'Sergio had seen the copy on her desk'. Acceptable medium.

DEFECT: question names the narrator 'Putri' but the first-person passage never gives a name — fix question stem ('the narrator'). D also differs in form (starts with 'Hari's story' not 'She'), which flags it.
'until she was satisfied that I would not lose it' makes A explicit. Passage only implies Esperanza is the grandmother; A says 'grandson' — acceptable but slightly inferential.
Somchai's explanation gives the motive almost verbatim; C uses 'face burned' as a trap but is weak. Easy.
A (exhaustion) is a good surface trap; the mother's-empty-chair memory decides D. Stray 'folktale tellers' line in a realist passage is odd.
Good weighting item: B/C invert the proportion, D is single-note. 'pushed the cutting board an inch farther' seals resentment as dominant. Strong medium, borderline hard.
C inverts the weighting plausibly; A/D weaker. Kite climbing at the end makes the hopeful turn fairly clear.
A and B are both proportion-wrong in opposite directions; requires tracking subtext across the whole poem. Good item, borderline hard.
